methodology.timing: Process wall in measurements; library wall excluding TPC-H pool initialization in library_measurements. Library timing includes table/session/job creation, worker startup/join, generation and batch consumption.
methodology.cpu_and_rss: Whole fresh process, including setup. Ordered Populate consumers run on the calling thread; reference partitions consume/drop on their workers. Reference comparisons therefore include delivery-semantics differences; before/after comparisons keep the ordered API.
methodology.output: Full Arrow RecordBatches are generated and consumed; no IPC encoding, file output, disk flushing or cache drops.
methodology.scale: TPC-H SF0.1/1/10/100; SSB and flat SSB SF1/10/100. Individual TPC-H tables at SF10, lineitem/orders at SF1/100. TPC-H all tables at 1/4/32 threads at SF10.
methodology.batch_defaults: Populate TPC-H/SSB 8192; Rust references 8000. All batch/chunk overrides zero.
methodology.reference: Rust tpchgen/tpchgen-arrow 4.0.0. The reference and candidate use the same final executable and allocator. Each reference table uses up to 32 source partitions.
methodology.aggregate: Selected tables follow TableName::ALL unless explicitly listed. The multi-thread reference adapter pops table/partition jobs from a shared Vec in LIFO order. Populate schedules remaining work per source and fuses compatible TPC-DS sales/returns. Aggregate speedups include scheduling and fusion differences; aggregate times cannot be obtained by adding isolated table times.
methodology.controls: stream consumes/drops each batch on its worker; TPC-DS stream is unfused. Do not attribute an ordered-fused versus stream-unfused difference solely to buffering.
methodology.sampling: Seven measured fresh processes after one excluded warmup per configuration. Baseline/candidate order alternates; no timing runs overlap builds, tests, full-output hashing or profiling.
methodology.noise: The schema-required noise_threshold of 0.1 is descriptive, not an adaptive stopping rule. The primary matrix always uses seven measured runs; mixed small-scale results receive separately reported follow-up comparisons. All samples, including outliers, are retained.
methodology.source: Main pinned at d959a113 when upstream native APIs arrived during the investigation. Final comparisons are rebuilt from that exact main and the rebased candidate. Earlier screens are recorded separately.
methodology.architecture: Measured on this 32-core AArch64 machine. Fused bounded fills and comment prefetching are AArch64-only; other architectures retain the previous RNG/comment implementation. Column appends apply on all architectures; no x86 speedup is claimed.

experiments.change: Map each 16-lane Lehmer block to bounded integers before storing it; preserve the last raw draw as stream state.
experiments.why: Avoids the separate bounding pass for AArch64 bounded streams. Seven-run removal experiments show an incremental aggregate improvement, especially SF100.
experiments.proof: Bitwise scalar/original-kernel comparisons cover empty/partial/multiple blocks, five seeds, signed and large ranges, continuation and skip. Final full-output hashes and reference tests cover integration.

experiments.change: Append each order's 1..7 line values column by column, sharing derived ship/receipt dates.
experiments.why: Exact-length appends check numeric capacity once per order; the output and RNG draw counts are unchanged.
experiments.proof: Existing reference, boundary, Arrow, text and Parquet tests; native-only tests after rebase; full SF10/SF100 output hashes.

experiments.change: Prefetch the immutable text-pool locations 32 comments ahead while building Arrow string views on AArch64.
experiments.why: Independent random prefix reads are a major sampled CPU cost. Seven-run removal comparisons show the largest incremental aggregate gain of these components.
experiments.proof: Compare every u128 view and actual Arrow text with scalar construction across short/long/empty strings and batch/cache/pool boundaries; full output hashes.

experiments.change: Increase the comment prefetch distance from 32 to 64.
experiments.why: No consistent additional improvement over the 32-ahead screen. Screens were separately interleaved with baseline, not a direct 32-vs-64 comparison.

experiments.change: Precompute exact u32 reciprocal division for part-supplier lookup.
experiments.why: ASM showed divisions, but removing them did not improve aggregate generation in three-run SF10/SF100 screens; extra arithmetic and code complexity were not justified.
experiments.proof: Boundary/random quotient tests and TPC-H reference tests passed, but performance did not.

experiments.decision: retain; final rebased comparisons and full output hashes pass
experiments.change: Compose bounded fills, per-column line appends and 32-ahead comment prefetching.
experiments.why: Individual effects interact, so the combined candidate is measured directly.

lessons: Do not add independently measured component percentages; use the combined comparison.
A sampled division is not evidence that replacing it will improve elapsed time.
Prove raw RNG continuation as well as generated values when fusing a transform into the RNG fill.
Prefetching is architecture and workload sensitive; no x86 performance claim is supported by this box.
Small-scale aggregate timings need repeated controls because scheduling overhead can dominate.
Pin both source trees and frozen binary hashes; rebase/API changes require fresh final measurements.
Completion markers must match exactly; an intermediate TIMINGS COMPLETE marker caused excluded follow-up timings to overlap hashing. The corrected independent repeats replace them.
A smaller flamegraph frame after a refactor can reflect outlined helper functions; compare aggregate counters and elapsed time before attributing a speedup.

future_work.idea: Share orders/lineitem RNG work across tables
future_work.potential: Avoid repeated draws and price/status derivations when both tables are generated together.
future_work.obstacles: Independent table selection, ordered delivery, deterministic skip-ahead and chunk ownership need a common paired source.
future_work.proof_required: All table combinations, thread/batch/scale boundaries, full reference equality, memory peaks and repeated aggregate/isolated timings.

future_work.potential: Carry bounded RNG vectors directly into pricing/date/flag columns.
future_work.obstacles: Exact integer semantics, variable line counts, architecture-specific code, and public native types constrain vectorization.
future_work.proof_required: Scalar oracle, continuation/skip tests, x86/ARM correctness and speed, ASM confirmation, multi-scale measurements.

future_work.idea: Remove remaining intermediate line stream buffers
future_work.potential: Reduce scratch writes and allocation between independent streams and final columns.
future_work.obstacles: The composable Distribution API promises typed native columns and independent collectors; a specialized path must preserve those contracts.
future_work.proof_required: Native/Arrow/text/Parquet equivalence and whole-framework benchmarks, not only a kernel microbenchmark.

final_findings.ci: [GitHub CI](https://github.com/joseph-isaacs/populate/actions/runs/45830194471) also passes formatting, Clippy, workspace tests, Python and MSRV on the PR integration commit.
limitations: No universal speedup is claimed: the 21-pair SF0.1 follow-up is 5.362→5.404 ms (+0.8%), with overlapping ranges. SF1 SSB is noisy: the primary matrix improves 5.7%, while the clean follow-up changes 13.396→13.788 ms (+2.9%) with broad overlapping ranges. Small TPC-H tables and flat SSB are also within their observed spread; the clearest gains are SF10/SF100 TPC-H.

Peak RSS is measured for whole fresh processes. At SF100, median all-table RSS is 1.83→1.87 GiB and isolated lineitem is 1.82→1.98 GiB. Timed generation writes no dataset files; full verification also streams its output in memory.

The first small-scale follow-up accidentally overlapped hashing because its completion check accepted an intermediate marker. Those trials are excluded and retained only for audit; the corrected follow-ups run after profiling. The primary seven-run matrix is unaffected.
profiles: The new comment assembly issues PRFM PLDL1KEEP at 0x4295a8, then reads the current Comment from pointer −256 bytes: 32 records of 8 bytes. The bounded RNG block mixes scalar multiply instructions with NEON reductions/packing; it is not a fully vectorized specialized kernel.

Fresh all-table SF100 perf stat shows 6.2% fewer user cycles and 1.9% fewer instructions; lineitem shows 5.8% fewer cycles and 2.1% fewer instructions. These are separate whole-process captures including setup/repeated generation, not replacements for the seven-run wall-time medians.

Reported cache misses fall about 53% for all tables and 56% for lineitem. Counters are multiplexed (roughly 49–75% running time), so these single captures are supporting evidence, not a precise causal attribution or repeatable cache-miss speedup.

Flamegraph leaf shares move across newly outlined functions. The lineitem FlatMap frame falls from 46.53% to 32.59%, but separate word/comment append loops appear; that frame change cannot be read as a 30% lineitem speedup. Comment view construction remains about a quarter of sampled cycles. All four fresh captures report zero lost samples.
learning: Keep fused bounds, per-column line appends and 32-ahead comment prefetching. Before the main rebase, seven-run component-removal comparisons at SF100 showed incremental elapsed-time reductions of 1.36%, 1.75% and 3.13%, respectively; do not add them. The final rebased combination is measured independently.
Reject reciprocal supplier division: output tests passed, but SF10/SF100 aggregate screens did not improve. Do not mistake a visible division in ASM for a worthwhile optimization.
Do not select 64-ahead prefetching: separately interleaved screens showed no consistent extra gain over 32. No direct 32-vs-64 speedup is claimed.
Prove raw RNG state and skip behavior, not just the values in one batch; preserve native/Arrow feature combinations when rebasing.

More complex remaining opportunities: share orders/lineitem streams across tables, use architecture-specific SIMD pricing/date kernels, and remove intermediate line-stream buffers. These require deterministic partitioning, exact-value oracles, API/ownership work, and new measurements; none is claimed as an achieved gain.

specification.validation_scope: Full ordered text serialization of generated Arrow batches is SHA-256 compared against the pinned main for all eight TPC-H tables at SF10 and SF100, all five SSB tables and the flat table at SF10. Generator tests additionally compare with Rust references, text, Parquet and native output. Performance samples validate row counts; hashes are separate untimed comparisons.
specification.profile_interpretation: Whole-process user-cycle samples include setup and repeated generation, amortizing initialization relative to fresh-process timings. Flame widths are sampled cycle weights, not elapsed time or promised speedups. perf stat runs separately; retain counter multiplex percentages.

investigation_before_rebase.note: Exploratory three-run individual screens and seven-run component-removal comparisons precede the final main rebase. Do not combine their medians with final measurements or add component percentage effects. Component-removal baseline means the combined candidate without the named component; candidate means the full combination. Interrupted final-run timings are excluded.

excluded_followup_trials.reason: The first follow-up runner incorrectly treated TIMINGS COMPLETE as the final COMPLETE marker and overlapped output hashing. Primary timing trials were already finished and are unaffected.
